name: Bi Luo Chun

origin.regionNote: 洞庭 on Taihu, Jiangsu — not the Hunan lake

pluckStandard: one bud and one tiny leaf, extremely fine

processing.description: Minute buds picked around orchards of peach, plum and loquat.
Brief indoor wither before the wok, as with Long Jing.
Gentle pan-fire; fruit-blossom aromatics from neighbouring trees cling to the downy buds.
Rolled into tight spirals — the “green snails”. The fork with Long Jing is this shape, not the fire.
Finished at low heat so the white pekoe remains visible.

profile.mouthfeel: delicate, slightly viscous from the down

infusions.notes: leaves can be dropped onto water to watch them unfurl

water.note: Very soft water; high mineral content flattens the floral top.

storage: Refrigerate sealed if keeping past early summer. Hygroscopic down picks up fridge smells — double-bag.

qualityMarkers.claim: intense floral hit on dry leaf

commonFaults.name: large coarse leaf sold as Bi Luo Chun

summary: Downy spiral greens from Taihu orchards, famous for a floral, fruity lift unusual among pan-fired greens.

compare.differentiator: Same pan-fire class; Long Jing is flattened in the wok, not spiralled, and grows at Xi Hu, not Taihu.
